Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office maintains standardized intake files, assigning each submission a unique case identifier. Documents are scanned, indexed by applicant reference number, and filed into designated categories. Cross-references link supporting materials to primary forms, with all entries timestamped and stored in the central filing system.

2) What occurred: The actor prepared Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative, with the relationship field recorded as "spouse," attaching a dated marriage certificate bearing a registry number. A joint lease agreement, a bank account statement, and dated photographs were filed as supporting evidence under category "proof of cohabitation." The actor transmitted a wire transfer receipt, recorded as a "loan," between the two named parties. Interview preparation notes, listing anticipated questions and scripted responses, were stored in the actor's file. A second document, marked confidential, detailed a payment schedule to a named third party.

3) Materials/access observed: One marriage certificate with a registry number and date; one lease agreement listing both parties as occupants; one bank statement showing the transfer; one set of dated photographs; one payment schedule; one interview preparation document. All items were filed under the primary case identifier in the joint-evidence folder.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The marriage certificate date and the first cohabitation evidence date were separated by less than 30 days. The bank statement showed a transfer matching the amount in the payment schedule. The interview preparation document contained identical phrasing to the responses given in the recorded interview. The payment schedule referenced a third party not listed on any filed document. The joint evidence folder contained no documents predating the petition filing.
